content.comment_body: Hello, I have the following components: [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]), [product_name] Communication Module, and a BEIJER VFD (BFI-E3-12-0023-1F12). I want to control a standard squirrel cage motor using Modbus, such as starting, stopping, and changing the direction of rotation. Does anyone have links to relevant projects, websites, or advice for this setup? Thanks in advance.
Your [product_name] [version_no] supports Modbus TCP/IP, but the BEIJER VFD you mentioned only works with Modbus RTU. You will need a gateway that translates Modbus RTU to Modbus TCP/IP.

Thank you for your input. Am I correct in understanding that the Communication Module I referred to operates only as a switch? If so, what are its benefits compared to a regular switch? Would switching to Micromaster VFDs address this issue? Any recommendations for a gateway compatible with the Beijer VFD? Thank you.

Micromaster won't solve the issue if the drive doesn't support Modbus/TCP. Consider replacing the Communication Module with another module that supports protocol conversion; the switch is only for networking, while the converter module offers serial communication and can handle Modbus RTU. Please note, I don't have direct experience with the protocol converter module. Alternatively, you could use traditional discrete wiring, or switch to a different PLC model.
I want to show my students a modern installation. After speaking with Beijer, I plan to buy a VFD with Ethernet connectivity from them. Thank you for your time and assistance.
Wishing you success! We can discuss later whether IIOT control represents the future. {wink}
Hello :-) Were you able to solve controlling your VFD via Ethernet or bus from your [product_name]? br

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to control a VFD through [product_name] using Modbus communication and face incompatibility between Modbus TCP/IP and Modbus RTU standards. There is uncertainty about the features of various Communication Modules, particularly regarding switching and protocol conversion capabilities. Recommendations focus on using gateways or choosing alternative hardware that is natively compatible. Users aim for up-to-date teaching setups, but encounter gaps in accessible documentation and intuitive hardware selection for educational demonstrations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek straightforward Modbus communication between [product_name] and the VFD to manage motor control functions for educational purposes. They expect intuitive options for module selection and protocol conversion within the same product family.
